newsitem.title: UK: Charterers advised to hedge rising tanker rates.
newsitem.headline: Charterers advised to hedge rising tanker rates.

text.p: Tanker charterers are being recommended by an independent shipping consultancy to seek timecharter cover for the next two years to hedge against climbing rates, particularly for modern VLCCs.

Maritime Strategies International Ltd (MSI) said one year time charter earnings are expected to climb to at least $32,500 a day for modern VLCCs by the end of the year with spot market spikes taking daily rates to almost $40,000 in the interim.

In its latest Freight Forecaster monthly report, the consultants said that as a result, "MSI is recommending that charterers seek immediate cover...but will be strongly advising they limit their cover to two years plus options."

MSI said it was "unashamedly optimistic" about short-term prospects for crude carrier earnings as aggregate oil demand was rising three percent year on year while fleet growth would be negligible over the next six months.
Alongside other market analysts MSI sees tanker markets peaking in 1998 but coming down again in 1999 and 2000.
The London-based analysts added that they were not alarmed by current growing tanker orderbooks.
MSI said: "More critical is the speed with which charterer attitudes shift against 20 year-old vessels."
MSI added it would become concerned at speculative tanker ordering if chartering policy did not harden against older ships.
-- Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
